paragraphs: Some prediction tasks come with rules about which output labels are compatible. Such rules offer information beyond individual training examples: a network can produce plausible labels separately while producing an inconsistent combination. This paper develops a training formulation that incorporates a supplied set of hard rules about output labels.

The method first translates those rules into soft logical constraints on the probability distributions produced by the network. It then expresses training as an alternating minimization and maximization problem, with a Lagrangian variable associated with each constraint. This connects learning the network parameters with accounting for violations of the supplied rules.

Because the constraints do not depend on knowing an example’s target labels, the formulation also extends to semi-supervised learning. Experiments cover semantic role labeling, named entity recognition, and fine-grained entity typing. The authors report substantially fewer constraint violations and show that the approach can also achieve state-of-the-art predictive performance. The findings support using output relationships as useful training information, alongside labeled examples.
neurips-2019-a-primal-dual-formulation-f.tldr: A constrained training formulation incorporates output-label rules into neural networks, reducing violations and sometimes achieving state-of-the-art performance.

paragraphs: Object detection requires learning both what an object is and where it appears. Preparing training data therefore involves drawing bounding boxes around individual objects, which makes large annotated datasets expensive to produce. This paper proposes Consistency-based Semi-supervised learning for object Detection, or CSD, to improve detection by using available images without those annotations.

The central idea is to apply consistency constraints to both parts of the detection task: object classification and localization. Unlabeled data can therefore contribute training signals about predicted categories as well as predicted positions. Extending consistency to localization matters because agreement about an object’s category alone does not address the full detection problem.

The method also introduces Background Elimination to address the harmful influence of background regions, which predominate in detection data. The authors evaluate CSD with both single-stage and two-stage detectors and report effective results in both settings. Their findings support combining consistency across detection outputs with explicit treatment of background when using unlabeled images.
neurips-2019-consistency-based-semi-supe.tldr: CSD uses consistency in object categories and locations, together with background elimination, to improve detection with unlabeled images.

paragraphs: A signal can contain several sinusoidal components, each with its own frequency. Frequency estimation seeks to identify those frequencies from a limited collection of noisy measurements. The problem appears in applications such as radar imaging, underwater acoustics, seismic imaging, and spectroscopy, where the observed samples must reveal the signal’s underlying components.

The paper builds on a learning approach that represents candidate frequencies through peaks in a neural network’s output. It introduces a new architecture that produces a substantially more accurate representation. A second neural network module estimates how many frequencies are present, addressing a separate part of the task needed to turn the representation into a complete estimate.

Together, the two modules form a fast, fully automatic frequency estimation method. The authors report state-of-the-art results, with particularly substantial improvements over existing techniques at medium-to-high noise levels. The contribution combines better identification of frequency locations with a learned estimate of component count, allowing the system to address both questions within one method.
neurips-2019-data-driven-estimation-of-s.tldr: Two neural network modules jointly estimate sinusoid frequencies and their number, with especially strong reported results under medium-to-high noise.

paragraphs: Neural architecture design often starts with a limited set of manually chosen building blocks. Even architecture search can restrict which connections are possible. Discovering Neural Wirings expands this design space by allowing channels to establish connections independently, relaxing the usual organization of a network into fixed layers.

The method learns connectivity while it learns the network’s parameters. Its structure can therefore change during training, and it discovers sparse subnetworks within predefined architectures in a single training run. Although each forward pass uses only a small fraction of the weights, the possible combinations provide a large space of candidate subnetworks.

Experiments show that the learned connections outperform the hand-designed and randomly connected networks considered by the authors. They also demonstrate that the approach extends to recurrent and continuous-time networks. The work connects architecture search with sparse network learning: at sufficiently fine granularity, choosing an architecture becomes closely related to choosing which connections remain active.
neurips-2019-discovering-neural-wirings-.tldr: Discovering Neural Wirings learns sparse channel connections alongside network weights, improving on the hand-designed and random connections tested.

paragraphs: When reinforcement learning must use a fixed dataset, a new policy may encounter states and actions in different proportions from those represented in the data. Discounted stationary distribution ratios describe that mismatch. They compare how frequently the new policy would experience a state-action pair with how frequently that pair appears in the dataset.

DualDICE estimates these correction quantities without requiring knowledge of the behavior policy, or collection of policies, that generated the data. It also avoids directly using importance weights. This design sidesteps potential optimization instabilities associated with direct importance weighting in previous methods, while addressing the distribution differences relevant to evaluating or training a new policy.

The paper supplies theoretical guarantees and evaluates the algorithm empirically for off-policy policy evaluation. In that study, DualDICE significantly improves estimation accuracy over existing techniques. The findings support its use for correcting dataset-policy mismatch in evaluation; the broader motivation also includes training policies when fresh interaction with the environment is unavailable.
neurips-2019-dualdice-behavior-agnostic-.tldr: DualDICE estimates policy-to-dataset distribution corrections without knowing the data-collection policies, improving off-policy evaluation accuracy in experiments.

paragraphs: Graph Recurrent Attention Networks, or GRANs, generate a graph by adding blocks of nodes and their associated edges. Block size and sampling stride provide controls for trading sample quality against computational efficiency. This approach addresses the long sequences involved when graph generation relies on recurrent models.

A graph neural network with attention connects the already generated graph to the part being generated next. The authors report that this better captures the required conditioning, reduces dependence on node ordering, and avoids the long-term bottleneck of recurrent generation. Within each block, a mixture of Bernoulli distributions represents correlations among generated edges.

The method also accounts for multiple canonical node orderings by marginalizing over them, instead of relying on just one ordering. On standard benchmarks, the authors report state-of-the-art generation speed and sample quality relative to previous models. They additionally demonstrate good-quality generation of graphs containing up to 5,000 nodes, supporting the framework’s ability to handle larger graph outputs.
neurips-2019-efficient-graph-generation-.tldr: GRAN generates graphs in blocks using attention and correlated edge predictions, achieving strong reported quality and efficiency at sizes up to 5,000 nodes.

paragraphs: Image augmentation changes the training examples seen by a classifier, but it can also create a mismatch in apparent object size between training and testing. This paper identifies a substantial discrepancy of that kind. In the settings studied, lowering the training resolution can improve classification at test time.

The proposed strategy deliberately uses different resolutions for training and testing, then performs computationally inexpensive fine-tuning at the intended test resolution. This makes it possible to conduct training with smaller images while adapting the classifier to the resolution at which it will be evaluated. The authors report that this substantially reduces training time while retaining strong classification performance.

For ResNet-50, the reported ImageNet top-1 accuracies are 77.1% with training images of 128 by 128 pixels and 79.8% with training at 224 by 224. The method also improves a weakly supervised, pretrained ResNeXt model. These results highlight resolution choice and subsequent adaptation as consequential parts of the training procedure, beyond simply selecting a network architecture.
neurips-2019-fixing-the-train-test-resol.tldr: Training with smaller images and cheaply fine-tuning at test resolution addresses object-size mismatch and yields strong classification results.

paragraphs: This paper studies generalization in deep networks whose hidden layers contain far more units than there are training examples. The focus is a sufficiently wide ReLU network trained by stochastic gradient descent from random initialization. The theoretical question is how to bound its expected classification error.

The authors relate that error to the training loss of a simpler random feature model constructed from the network’s gradients at initialization. They call this the neural tangent random feature model. This comparison connects the trained network’s predictive behavior with features determined at its starting point, providing a way to analyze generalization through the associated feature model.

For data distributions that this feature model can classify with sufficiently small error, the resulting generalization bound scales approximately as the inverse square root of the number of examples, up to logarithmic factors. The bound does not depend on network width, although sufficient width remains an assumption. The paper also establishes a close connection with the neural tangent kernel and reports sharper, more general bounds than many existing results.
neurips-2019-generalization-bounds-of-st.tldr: For sufficiently wide ReLU networks and suitably classifiable data, an initialization-based feature model yields a width-independent generalization bound.

paragraphs: A neural network layer may contain many units while its responses to data vary along far fewer underlying dimensions. This paper studies that intrinsic dimension: the minimum number of parameters needed to describe a representation. The aim is to understand the geometry of data as trained networks transform it across layers.

The authors find intrinsic dimensions orders of magnitude below the number of units in a layer. Across the network, intrinsic dimension initially rises and then progressively falls toward the final layers. They also find that the intrinsic dimension of the last hidden layer predicts classification accuracy on held-out test data.

These patterns do not appear with linear dimension estimates such as principal component analysis, or after artificially linearizing the representations. They are also absent in untrained networks and networks trained on randomized labels. Together, the observations suggest that successful generalization is associated with transforming data into low-dimensional structures that may be curved. The evidence supports this geometric interpretation without establishing that low dimension alone causes generalization.
neurips-2019-intrinsic-dimension-of-data.tldr: The study links generalization to low-dimensional, potentially curved representations and finds that final hidden-layer dimension predicts test accuracy.

paragraphs: Graph matching seeks correspondences between graphs and is used in fields including computer vision, pattern recognition, and bioinformatics. Two standard mathematical formulations describe it as different quadratic assignment problems. This paper develops a common view of those formulations, creating a route to solving matching problems with less computational overhead.

The authors introduce rules for array operations in Hilbert spaces. Under this formulation, Lawler’s quadratic assignment problem becomes an alignment between two arrays in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, in the style of the Koopmans-Beckmann formulation. The practical benefit is that the method can avoid explicitly computing a huge affinity matrix.

The paper also introduces an entropy-regularized Frank-Wolfe optimization algorithm. It preserves the convergence rate of the original Frank-Wolfe method while greatly reducing computation per outer iteration. Extensive experiments show significant improvements over the state of the art in both matching accuracy and scalability. The contribution therefore combines a more economical representation of the matching problem with a less expensive optimization procedure.
neurips-2019-kergm-kernelized-graph-matc.tldr: KerGM unifies two graph-matching formulations and uses entropy-regularized optimization to improve reported accuracy and scalability.

paragraphs: This paper studies least-squares regression in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, a mathematical setting for learning flexible prediction functions. Its objective is to understand how accurately a randomized learning algorithm can predict under squared loss. The authors propose an algorithm with optimal generalization error bounds, closing a previously unresolved gap between upper and lower bounds.

The analysis also examines problems with small Bayes risk under squared loss. Bayes risk describes the error of the best possible predictor for the underlying problem. When that risk is small, the proposed algorithm has faster rates both at finite stages and asymptotically. This acceleration is explicitly tied to that favorable property of the problem.

The guarantees are expressed through two standard ingredients of kernel regression theory: how quickly the associated integral operator’s eigenvalues decay, and the complexity of the optimal predictor as measured through that operator. These ingredients specify the setting of the results. The contribution combines optimal generalization guarantees with a more favorable analysis for low-noise problems.
neurips-2019-kernel-truncated-randomized.tldr: A randomized kernel regression algorithm achieves optimal generalization bounds and faster rates when the problem’s squared-loss Bayes risk is small.

paragraphs: Instance segmentation on a 3D point cloud requires distinguishing individual objects and assigning points to them. The proposed 3D-BoNet framework tackles both object extent and point membership directly. It predicts a three-dimensional bounding box for every instance while also producing a point-level mask for each instance.

The architecture follows a design based on per-point multilayer perceptrons. A shared backbone feeds two parallel branches: one regresses bounding boxes, and the other predicts masks. The system is single-stage, uses no anchors, and can be trained end to end. It also avoids post-processing operations such as non-maximum suppression, feature sampling, clustering, and voting.

Experiments on ScanNet and S3DIS show that 3D-BoNet surpasses the existing work considered while being approximately ten times more computationally efficient. Ablation studies additionally support the effectiveness of its design. These findings show that directly learning boxes and masks together can provide an effective and computationally economical framework for the evaluated point-cloud segmentation tasks.
neurips-2019-learning-object-bounding-bo.tldr: 3D-BoNet jointly predicts object boxes and point masks, surpassing compared methods on two datasets with approximately tenfold computational efficiency.

paragraphs: Sparse coding is commonly solved through repeated optimization updates, including the Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm, or ISTA. Unfolded networks turn those updates into neural network layers and learn parameters to accelerate estimation. This paper investigates how much can be gained by learning only the step sizes used by ISTA.

The authors first show that a simple step-size strategy can improve ISTA’s convergence rate by using the sparsity of intermediate iterates. Because that strategy is impractical for most large-scale applications, they propose a network that learns the step sizes instead. This concentrates learning on the update size while retaining the underlying ISTA structure.

The paper also establishes a conditional structural result: for a broad class of unfolded algorithms, convergence to the Lasso solution implies that the final layers take the form of ISTA with learned step sizes. Experiments show competitive performance against state-of-the-art networks when the target solutions are sufficiently sparse. That qualification is central to the reported empirical effectiveness of the simpler architecture.
neurips-2019-learning-step-sizes-for-unf.tldr: Learning only ISTA step sizes yields a theoretically motivated unfolded network that is competitive when solutions are sufficiently sparse.

paragraphs: Local differential privacy constrains learning from data held by individual clients. Many efficient algorithms require repeated communication with a server, but network latency makes those rounds costly. This paper investigates the learning capabilities of non-interactive protocols, motivated by systems restricted to a single communication round.

The authors prove that margin complexity lower-bounds the complexity of non-interactive, locally private, distribution-independent PAC learning for Boolean function classes. In particular, learning linear separators and decision lists requires exponentially many samples without interaction, even though interactive locally private algorithms can learn them in polynomial time. This establishes a substantial separation for natural learning problems.

A complementary algorithm has complexity polynomial in margin complexity. It avoids interaction on labeled examples but still requires interactive access to unlabeled examples, so it does not remove interaction altogether. The results also apply to statistical query learning and models that limit the number of bits communicated about each data point. They clarify when communication restrictions can fundamentally change learning difficulty.
neurips-2019-locally-private-learning-wi.tldr: The paper proves exponential sample requirements for non-interactive locally private learning of certain natural classes that admit efficient interactive learning.

paragraphs: Recognizing facial action units supports emotion and mental-state analysis, but producing accurate action-unit labels requires expertise and time. This paper combines a small labeled face dataset with a large collection of unlabeled web images. Its semi-supervised approach draws on co-training while learning the different feature views within the model.

Two deep networks generate representations for labeled and unlabeled faces. A multi-view loss is designed to encourage conditionally independent representations, while a separate co-regularization loss brings the networks’ predicted action-unit probability distributions closer together. The method therefore seeks distinct representations that nonetheless agree about the action units present.

A graph convolutional network incorporates prior knowledge about relationships among action units, adding structure to how information from unlabeled images is used. Across several benchmarks, the authors report improved robustness and performance above the state-of-the-art semi-supervised methods considered. The findings support combining learned feature views, agreement between predictions, and known relationships among labels to make unlabeled face images useful for this recognition task.
neurips-2019-multi-label-co-regularizati.tldr: Two cooperating networks and a graph of action-unit relationships use unlabeled face images to improve semi-supervised recognition.

paragraphs: Machine learning commonly trains models by minimizing expected loss: an average of how costly their predictions are. This paper questions whether that objective adequately reflects human attitudes toward risk. Its motivation comes from behavioral economics, where human decision-making has been shown to follow risk measures that differ from expected loss.

The authors investigate a class of alternative risk measures inspired by cumulative prospect theory. They analyze properties of these objectives and ask whether optimizing them could better align learning with human preferences. The inquiry also considers fairness, examining the possibility that changing how losses are assessed could support goals beyond average predictive performance.

Empirical studies show improvements on desiderata such as fairness compared with conventional expected-loss minimization. The result gives evidence that the choice of risk measure can matter for these broader objectives. The paper’s claim remains qualified: the analyzed measures may offer better alignment, and the experiments demonstrate improvements in the studied settings rather than a universal guarantee of fairness.
neurips-2019-on-human-aligned-risk-minim.tldr: Risk measures inspired by cumulative prospect theory offer an alternative to expected loss and improve fairness-related outcomes in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Generating source code from natural-language specifications requires decisions at different levels. A system must capture the program’s overall patterns while also supplying implementation details. Patois addresses this combination by allowing a neural program synthesizer to interleave high-level and low-level reasoning throughout generation.

The system automatically extracts recurring code idioms from a supplied corpus. It adds those idioms to the language available to the synthesizer, then trains a tree-based neural model to use them when producing programs. Common patterns become explicit generation options, alongside the choices needed to express lower-level details. The idioms are learned from code rather than supplied solely as manually defined patterns.

The authors evaluate Patois on two complex semantic parsing datasets and find that learned idioms improve synthesis accuracy. This supports making recurring program structure available directly to the generator. The contribution is the combination of corpus-based idiom discovery and a synthesizer trained to mix those higher-level constructs with detailed program generation.
neurips-2019-program-synthesis-and-seman.tldr: Patois learns recurring code idioms and lets a neural synthesizer combine them with low-level generation, improving accuracy on two datasets.

paragraphs: Recommendation and retrieval models can embed queries and items into a shared low-dimensional space, using their inner product as a relevance score. Nonlinear inductive matrix completion learns those embeddings with neural networks. Analyzing it is challenging because both the nonlinear embeddings and the low-dimensional restriction introduce non-convexity.

This paper provides a theoretical analysis of a simple model with single-layer neural representations. It works in the realizable setting, where the ground-truth relevance scores come from the assumed model. Under the stated mild assumptions, gradient descent and stochastic gradient descent can recover the ground-truth parameters when initialized sufficiently close to the optimum.

The authors also show that a standard tensor method can provide the required initialization, connecting the local recovery guarantee to a way of obtaining a suitable starting point. The number of observed query-item relevance scores needed scales nearly linearly with input dimension, matching existing linear-model results. The guarantees thus establish recoverability for this specified nonlinear model under its assumptions and initialization conditions.
neurips-2019-provable-non-linear-inducti.tldr: A simple nonlinear query-item embedding model admits provable parameter recovery under realizability, suitable assumptions, and sufficiently close initialization.

paragraphs: Video interpolation synthesizes frames between recorded frames, helping overcome limits on how frequently a camera captures images. Many existing methods model motion as uniform between consecutive frames. This paper argues that such linear models poorly approximate the more complex movements that occur in real videos.

The proposed method uses a quadratic motion model that incorporates acceleration information. It can represent curved trajectories and changing velocity, giving the interpolation process a richer account of how scene content moves. This changes the motion assumption used to predict the missing frame, allowing more accurate results for the motions addressed by the method.

To synthesize high-quality images, the authors also introduce a flow reversal layer. It estimates motion fields directed from the unknown target frame back toward the source frames, and additional techniques refine those fields. Extensive experiments across a wide variety of video datasets show favorable performance against existing linear models. The contribution combines a more expressive motion model with components for turning that motion estimate into an interpolated frame.
neurips-2019-quadratic-video-interpolati.tldr: Quadratic video interpolation models acceleration and curved motion, producing favorable results against linear methods across varied video datasets.

paragraphs: Stochastic recurrent models with latent variables had shown strong results for sound-wave sequences, while ordinary recurrent networks often performed better elsewhere. This paper re-examines that discrepancy by looking at how earlier speech density-estimation comparisons represented dependencies within a single time step.

The authors find that a fully factorized output distribution imposed an unequal restriction. Stochastic models could implicitly exploit correlations among values within a step through their latent variables, while deterministic baselines could not. They revise the comparison so that every model can explicitly represent those correlations using an autoregressive output structure.

Across data including speech, MIDI music, handwriting trajectories, and frame-permuted speech, stochastic recurrent models no longer deliver the previously claimed advantage. Standard recurrent models with autoregressive outputs consistently perform better in the reported evaluation and substantially advance results on three speech datasets. The findings attribute the earlier comparison’s imbalance to unequal access to within-step correlations, changing how the observed benefit of latent variables should be interpreted.
neurips-2019-re-examination-of-the-role-.tldr: Allowing all models to represent within-step correlations removes the reported stochastic-model advantage and favors standard recurrent models in the evaluated tasks.

paragraphs: Robustness verification asks how much an input must change before a model’s prediction can be adversarially altered. For tree ensembles, verification can seek the exact smallest change or a guaranteed lower bound. This paper studies random forests and gradient-boosted trees, where exact mixed-integer optimization becomes impractical for large ensembles.

The authors give a finer account of the problem’s complexity. A single tree can be verified in linear time. Ensemble verification can be expressed as a maximum-clique problem on a multipartite graph with boxicity structure. For low-dimensional problems where boxicity is treated as constant, this yields a polynomial-time algorithm, despite the general problem being NP-complete.

For general cases, the proposed algorithm exploits that graph structure to compute robustness lower bounds. It can improve its bounds iteratively and stop at any time. Experiments report tighter bounds than a linear-programming relaxation and speeds hundreds of times faster than exact mixed-integer solving. The method also produces tight bounds for large boosted ensembles containing hundreds of deep trees.
neurips-2019-robustness-verification-of-.tldr: A graph-based formulation enables efficient robustness bounds for large tree ensembles and polynomial-time verification under a constant-boxicity condition.

paragraphs: Event order and elapsed time carry different information. Positional encoding lets self-attention distinguish where events occur in a sequence, but does not itself account for the gaps between them. This paper introduces a representation of time spans to help attention-based models capture temporal patterns alongside sequential order.

The method maps time spans into high-dimensional feature spaces. The authors construct an associated translation-invariant time kernel and use Bochner’s and Mercer’s theorems to derive functional forms for the feature map. This supplies a mathematical basis for representing elapsed time within the model, connecting the time features to kernel-based descriptions of temporal relationships.

The paper proposes several models that learn these time representations and their interactions with event representations. Evaluations use real-world datasets and multiple continuous-time event prediction tasks. The methods compare favorably with baseline models and capture useful interactions between timing and events. The findings support explicitly representing elapsed time when event sequences contain predictive temporal structure beyond their ordering.
neurips-2019-self-attention-with-functio.tldr: Kernel-derived time features help self-attention model elapsed time and useful time-event interactions in continuous-time prediction tasks.

paragraphs: Self-supervised tasks had been added to generative adversarial networks to help prevent the discriminator from forgetting learned information. This paper examines how those tasks affect the generator. Its analysis identifies a problem: a generator can perform very well on the self-supervised tasks while suffering severe mode collapse and producing limited diversity.

The authors propose replacement self-supervised tasks organized as a multi-class minimax game. Competition among these tasks encourages the generator to learn the data distribution and produce diverse outputs. The paper provides theoretical and empirical analyses supporting better convergence properties, connecting the auxiliary training tasks more directly to the intended behavior of the generator.

The tasks are incorporated into two GAN baselines. Experiments report state-of-the-art FID scores on six datasets, with considerable improvements in some cases. The unconditional model also approaches conditional GAN performance without labeled data. These findings support designing self-supervision around its interaction with generation, since success on an auxiliary task alone can coexist with poor output diversity.
neurips-2019-self-supervised-gan-analysi.tldr: A multi-class minimax formulation addresses self-supervised tasks that tolerate mode collapse and improves reported GAN convergence and generation quality.

paragraphs: Predicting pedestrian movement requires accounting for interactions among people and with their surroundings. A scene can also admit several plausible future paths for each person. Social-BiGAT addresses this combination by generating multiple realistic trajectory possibilities for interacting pedestrians, rather than treating the future as a single outcome.

A graph attention network learns features that encode social interactions among people in the scene. A recurrent encoder-decoder then uses those features to predict paths and is trained adversarially. These components connect the representation of interpersonal interactions with the generation of future movement.

To explicitly represent multiple possible futures, the framework forms a reversible transformation between each scene and its latent noise vector, following the Bicycle-GAN approach. This gives the latent representation a defined relationship with the scene in the trajectory generation process. Evaluations against several baselines on established trajectory forecasting benchmarks show state-of-the-art performance. The results support combining social interaction features with a generative model that explicitly accounts for multiple plausible trajectories.
neurips-2019-social-bigat-multimodal-tra.tldr: Social-BiGAT combines graph attention and adversarial trajectory generation to model social interactions and multiple plausible pedestrian futures.

paragraphs: Capsule networks can represent changes in an object’s viewpoint, making them useful for image classification. Their recurrent dynamic routing, however, carries substantial computational cost and makes large-scale use challenging. STAR-Caps changes the routing mechanism to address that bottleneck while retaining a capsule-based network.

The method uses attention modules augmented with differentiable binary routers to estimate routing coefficients without recurrence. The routers use straight-through estimators to decide whether a connection between capsules is active or inactive. This replaces repeated routing calculations with an attentive mechanism that makes explicit connection decisions, supporting the stable and faster performance described by the authors.

Experiments evaluate the network on MNIST, SmallNorb, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet. STAR-Caps outperforms the baseline capsule networks in these evaluations. The contribution shows that changing how capsules communicate can improve their practical performance, with routing itself serving as the main design target. Its reported evidence spans both smaller image classification datasets and the larger-scale ImageNet setting.
neurips-2019-star-caps-capsule-networks-.tldr: STAR-Caps replaces recurrent capsule routing with attentive binary connection decisions, delivering faster performance and better results than evaluated capsule baselines.
